business_model.basis: stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business section
business_model.claim: Ames National Corporation is a bank holding company whose sole material business is owning six community banks in central, north-central and south-central Iowa, serving small-to-medium businesses, individuals, and public entities in those regions.
quotes: The Company does not engage in any material business activities apart from its ownership of its banking subsidiaries and the management of its own loan portfolios.

All of the Company's operations are conducted in the State of Iowa and primarily within the central, north-central and south-central Iowa counties of Boone, Clarke, Hancock, Marshall, Polk, Story, Taylor and Union where the Company's banking subsidiaries are located.
The Banks focus on small-to-medium size businesses that traditionally wish to develop an exclusive relationship with a single bank.

business_model.basis: stated in both the 10-K and the 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: The largest component of net income is net interest income, defined as the spread between interest earned on earning assets (primarily loans and investments) and interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities (primarily deposits and other borrowings).
quotes: The largest component contributing to the Company's net income is net interest income, which is the difference between interest earned on earning assets (primarily loans and investments) and interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities (primarily deposit accounts and other borrowings).

The increase in earnings is primarily due to an increase in net interest income. Net interest income increased due to higher yields and average balances on investments, combined with a lower cost of funds driven by declining market rates and reduced borrowings.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business section
business_model.claim: The loan portfolio is composed of approximately 51% commercial, 23% agricultural, 25% 1-4 family residential, and 1% consumer loans.
quotes: Approximately 51% of the loan portfolio consists of loans made for commercial purposes.
Approximately 23% of the loan portfolio consists of loans made for agricultural purposes.
Approximately 25% of the loan portfolio consists of loans made for 1-4 family residential purposes.
Approximately 1% of the loan portfolio consists of loans made for consumer purposes.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1; the income statement in F2 shows noninterest income of $5,487 (thousands) for the six months ended June 30, 2026
business_model.claim: Noninterest income comes from wealth management fees, service charges on deposit accounts, merchant and card fees, gains on sale of loans held for sale, and securities gains or losses.
quotes: The principal sources of Company revenue are: (i) interest and fees earned on loans made or held by the Company and Banks; (ii) interest on investments, primarily on bonds, held by the Banks; (iii) fees on wealth management services; (iv) service charges on deposit accounts maintained at the Banks; (v) merchant and card fees; (vi) gain on the sale of loans; and (vii) securities gains (losses).

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K and the Q3 2026 earnings release

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q and 8-K MD&A; the structural maturity mismatch is described in the 10-K risk factors
business_model.claim: The company's revenue is sensitive to the direction of market interest rates: declining rates reduce deposit and borrowing costs (lowering interest expense) while the investment portfolio, with longer maturities, retains higher yields, widening the net interest margin.
quotes: Net interest income increased due to higher yields and average balances on investments, combined with a lower cost of funds driven by declining market rates and reduced borrowings.

The Company's earning assets (primarily its loan and investment portfolio) have longer maturities than its interest-bearing liabilities (primarily deposits and other borrowings); therefore, in a rising interest rate environment, interest expense will tend to increase more quickly than interest income as the interest-bearing liabilities reprice more quickly than earning assets, resulting in a reduction in net interest income.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors; current loss levels from the Q3 2026 8-K
business_model.claim: The company's agricultural loan exposure (approximately 23% of the portfolio) is a key credit-risk driver, with borrowers affected by commodity prices, input costs, weather, and trade/tariff policy.
quotes: A significant portion of our loan portfolio consists of loans to borrowers who are directly or indirectly affected by the health of the Iowa agricultural economy, which has recently been under stress due to low commodity and livestock prices, higher input costs caused by inflation and potential losses of foreign markets due to disruptions in trade relationships.
